bull.b: Consistent, high top-line growth (49% reported) indicates durable demand for Alarum’s cybersecurity and privacy offerings. Multi-year revenue expansion supports scale economics, recurring subscription monetization and reinvestment capacity, strengthening long-term growth optionality and product adoption.

Very low leverage and a strengthened equity base give the company financial flexibility to fund operations, product development or legal/regulatory responses without heavy reliance on external financing. This cushioning improves resilience across multi-month operational shocks.

bull.t: Scale and strategic shift to AI infrastructure
bull.b: Rapid Q1 growth and large infrastructure scale (50+ petabytes, 850 customers) plus a deliberate move toward larger AI infrastructure accounts signal a structural repositioning into higher-volume, higher-value use cases. bear.t: Deteriorating cash generation and margin compression
bear.b: A swing to negative operating and free cash flow in 2025, alongside a sharp net margin decline, signals weakening earnings quality and potential working-capital or operational stress. Persistent negative cash generation would constrain reinvestment, increase financing reliance, and undermine sustainable growth.

bear.t: Regulatory action and operational disruption from FBI domain seizures
bear.b: U.S. law‑enforcement domain seizures and resulting service pauses create structural operational and compliance risk for the proxy business. Prolonged regulatory scrutiny can limit service availability, increase monitoring costs, and erode customer trust and contract continuity over quarters.

bear.t: Ongoing litigation and potential class/derivative claims
bear.b: Active discovery, derivative and class‑action motions alleging disclosure failures create extended legal and governance uncertainty. Potential liabilities, higher compliance costs and management distraction could materially affect capital allocation, corporate governance and stakeholder confidence over the medium term.
